edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource (from Three Hundred Tang Poems).
edition.zh: 据维基文库（《唐诗三百首》本）。

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died around 779.
basis.zh: 唐诗，作者约卒于 779 年。

note.en: Zhang Ji is remembered almost entirely for this poem, and the temple outside Suzhou is remembered partly because of it; people still gather there on New Year’s Eve to hear the bell. The poem moves from sight to sound, and ends on a bell carrying across water to one sleepless person.
note.zh: 张继几乎只因这一首诗被记住，苏州城外的寒山寺也部分因它而闻名；至今每逢除夕，仍有人去那里听钟。诗从所见写到所闻，最后是一声钟响，越过水面，传到一个无眠的人耳边。

excerpt.orig: 姑蘇城外寒山寺，夜半鐘聲到客船。
excerpt.en: Outside the walls of Gusu, from Cold Mountain Temple, / the midnight bell reaches the traveller’s boat.
excerpt.zh: 姑苏城外寒山寺，夜半钟声到客船。

gloss.en: Frost fills the sky: the bitter cold of the night. The ancients thought frost fell from the sky.
gloss.zh: 霜满天：形容夜寒彻骨。古人以为霜从天降。

gloss.en: Maples by the water. Maple Bridge crosses the canal west of Suzhou.
gloss.zh: 江枫：江边的枫树。枫桥在今苏州城西。

gloss.en: Gusu, an old name for Suzhou, after Gusu Hill nearby.
gloss.zh: 姑苏：苏州的别称，因城西南有姑苏山而得名。

gloss.en: Cold Mountain Temple, near Maple Bridge, said to be named after the Tang poet-monk Hanshan.
gloss.zh: 寒山寺：在苏州城西枫桥附近，相传因唐代诗僧寒山曾住此而得名。

gloss.en: Ouyang Xiu doubted that temple bells were rung at midnight; later writers showed that some Tang temples did ring them.
gloss.zh: 欧阳修曾怀疑半夜不是打钟的时候，后人考证唐代确有寺院半夜鸣钟。
